description:
As a data engineer, you are monitoring ETL pipeline runs and need to analyze an existing log file to quickly identify any pipeline failures. In the directory /home/user/etl_logs/, there is a text file named pipeline_run.log which contains multiple lines corresponding to different ETL jobs, each line in the following format:

[TIMESTAMP] ETL_JOB_NAME - STATUS

Where:
  • TIMESTAMP is a datetime in ISO 8601 format (e.g. 2024-06-29T14:23:57Z)
  • ETL_JOB_NAME is a string without spaces (e.g. user_import, sales_transform)
  • STATUS is either SUCCESS or FAILED
Your task is to output a list of all ETL jobs that have failed, formatted as one job name per line, sorted alphabetically, and do not include duplicates (even if a job failed more than once). The output should only contain job names (ETL_JOB_NAME), nothing else. For example, if pipeline_run.log contains: 
[2024-06-29T14:23:57Z] user_import - FAILED
[2024-06-29T14:25:01Z] sales_transform - SUCCESS
[2024-06-29T14:27:42Z] user_import - SUCCESS
[2024-06-29T14:29:10Z] payment_load - FAILED
Your output should be: 
payment_load
user_import
Please perform the required analysis and output the results as specified.
truth:
The file /home/user/etl_logs/pipeline_run.log exists and contains the following text:

[2024-06-29T14:23:57Z] user_import - FAILED
[2024-06-29T14:25:01Z] sales_transform - SUCCESS
[2024-06-29T14:27:42Z] user_import - SUCCESS
[2024-06-29T14:29:10Z] payment_load - FAILED
[2024-06-29T14:31:10Z] product_transform - FAILED
[2024-06-29T14:33:11Z] sales_transform - FAILED
[2024-06-29T14:35:11Z] payment_load - SUCCESS

The correct output will be (sorted, job names only, no duplicates):

payment_load
product_transform
sales_transform
user_import

There are no permissions restrictions on /home/user/etl_logs/pipeline_run.log; user can read it.
